name: Cyanocobalamin
route_note: IM or deep SC injection for pernicious anaemia; high-dose oral or nasal spray for maintenance
originator: isolated by Merck (Karl Folkers' group) and Glaxo (Lester Smith)

discovery.by: Edward Rickes, Karl Folkers and colleagues (Merck); E. Lester Smith (Glaxo)
discovery.note: Red crystalline vitamin B12 was isolated from liver as the anti-pernicious anaemia factor; cyanocobalamin is the stable form produced during purification.

rx_status: OTC (oral); prescription for injection in many countries
tagline: Synthetic vitamin B12 that cures pernicious anaemia
summary: Cyanocobalamin is a stable synthetic form of vitamin B12 that the body converts into the active coenzymes methylcobalamin and adenosylcobalamin. It treats and prevents B12 deficiency, including pernicious anaemia, where loss of intrinsic factor prevents absorption from food.
mechanism: Vitamin B12 is a cobalt-containing corrinoid. Methylcobalamin is the cofactor for methionine synthase, which regenerates methionine from homocysteine and releases tetrahydrofolate for DNA synthesis. Adenosylcobalamin is the cofactor for methylmalonyl-CoA mutase in odd-chain fatty-acid and amino-acid metabolism.

Deficiency causes megaloblastic anaemia through folate trapping and impaired DNA synthesis, and neurological damage including subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord. Dietary B12 needs gastric intrinsic factor for ileal uptake; injected or very high oral doses bypass this requirement, as about 1% is absorbed by passive diffusion.
uses: Vitamin B12 deficiency from malabsorption, gastrectomy, diet or medicines such as metformin
Prevention of deficiency in vegans and older adults

history.title: Liver therapy
history.detail: George Minot and William Murphy show that eating raw liver cures pernicious anaemia.

history.title: Nobel Prize
history.detail: Whipple, Minot and Murphy receive the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for liver therapy.

history.title: Isolation
history.detail: Vitamin B12 is crystallised independently at Merck and Glaxo.

history.title: Structure solved
history.detail: Dorothy Hodgkin determines the structure of vitamin B12 by X-ray crystallography.

history.title: Hodgkin's Nobel
history.detail: Hodgkin receives the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, partly for the B12 structure.

history.title: Total synthesis
history.detail: Robert Woodward and Albert Eschenmoser complete the total synthesis of vitamin B12.

history.title: Nasal gel
history.detail: FDA approves intranasal cyanocobalamin (Nascobal gel), later replaced by a spray.

pk.half_life: about 6 days in plasma; body stores last years
pk.bioavailability: intrinsic-factor-dependent for dietary doses; about 1% passive absorption at high oral doses
pk.metabolism: converted to methylcobalamin and adenosylcobalamin; stored in liver
pk.excretion: bile with enterohepatic recycling; urine after injection

serious: hypokalaemia early in treatment of severe megaloblastic anaemia
pulmonary oedema and heart failure early in treatment

facts: Vitamin B12 is made only by bacteria and archaea; animals obtain it from food or symbiotic microbes, which is why vegans need supplements.
Commercial vitamin B12 is produced by bacterial fermentation, for example with Pseudomonas denitrificans.
